description: Scenarios every evaluated configuration must cover. A configuration either executes a scenario or reports it as unsupported with a reason. 'attacker_capability' says what the attacker is assumed to be able to do; a configuration's own trust assumptions are recorded in results.json.

scenarios.name: approved plan
scenarios.description: The plan that was reviewed and approved is applied unchanged.

scenarios.name: substituted plan
scenarios.attacker_capability: can replace the stored plan after approval and before apply
scenarios.description: A different plan is put where the approved plan was, and the executor is asked to apply it under the existing approval.

scenarios.name: re-plan after approval
scenarios.attacker_capability: can start a new plan for the same change after approval and ask the executor to apply it
scenarios.description: A new plan is created through the normal planning step after the approval, and the executor is asked to apply it under the earlier approval.

scenarios.name: different agent
scenarios.attacker_capability: can run the apply step under another workload identity
scenarios.description: The approved plan is executed by an agent other than the one the approval names.

scenarios.name: expired approval
scenarios.attacker_capability: can present an approval after it was meant to lapse
scenarios.description: The approved plan is executed after the approval's expiry time.

scenarios.name: self-approval
scenarios.attacker_capability: the requester can approve their own change
scenarios.description: The person or agent that requested the change is also recorded as its approver.

scenarios.name: no approval
scenarios.attacker_capability: can ask the executor to apply with no approval
scenarios.description: The executor is asked to apply a plan for which no approval exists.
